title: werk core.disclosure — machine-readable facts about synthetic content
description: BASE DOCTRINE: this node family belongs to every werk profile. It carries FACTS about how a work came to exist — was it AI-generated, by what, with what human involvement, with what markers, under what training-data statement. THE FORMAT SHIPS FACTS; THE VIEWER APPLIES JURISDICTION. There is no enforcement anywhere in this schema or in the format around it: no locks, no DRM, no mandatory viewer behaviour, no policy gate, no field that a conformant reader is obliged to obey. Anyone with a compiler may write a viewer that ignores every value in this file, and that freedom is intentional and constitutional — it is what 'open and clean' means. The format's only MUST-level demands are about honest READING and REPORTING, and they are in SPEC.md section 3.12. What a viewer then DOES is the viewer's responsibility under its own local law, and never the format's.

ai_generated.description: true when a generative model produced the content of this work, in whole or in part. This is a FACT ABOUT PRODUCTION, not a judgement about the result and not a legal conclusion. A reader that finds this key MUST report it as it stands; a reader that does not find this NODE reports 'no disclosure recorded', which is a different sentence from 'not AI-generated' and must not be collapsed into it.

ai_modified.description: true when a generative model altered content it did not create — an inpaint, an upscale, a style transfer over a photograph. A work can be ai_modified without being ai_generated, and the distinction is the one most often lost when this is squeezed into a single boolean.

generation_scope.description: How much of the work the model made. 'whole-work': everything a consumer sees came out of a model. 'partial': some of it did, and 'scope_note' says which parts. 'none': no generative model was involved in the content (a package may still carry a disclosure node saying exactly that, and saying it explicitly is worth more than staying silent).

scope_note.description: REQUIRED when generation_scope is 'partial'. Which parts, in plain language.

declared_by.description: Who is making these statements. A disclosure is an assertion by a party, not an emanation from the bytes, and a reader is entitled to know whose assertion it is. Where a signature chain exists (law 7) it is what binds this claim to that party; where it does not, this is a name and nothing more, and a tool MUST NOT present it as verified.

uri.description: Resolvable identity, matching a SIGNATURE.json signer uri where one exists.

recipe_node.description: node_id of the core.recipe that backs these statements, when there is one. A disclosure with a recipe beside it is checkable; a disclosure alone is a claim. Both are legal.

models.description: The models involved, as facts. This duplicates part of core.recipe ON PURPOSE (law 9, every payload serves two masters): a listing tool showing 'made with X' should not have to parse a full reproduction record, and a package may carry a disclosure without carrying a recipe at all. Where both exist they MUST agree, and a reader that finds them disagreeing reports it rather than picking one.

version_note.description: Hosted model ids are not versions: the weights behind a stable id may change without notice. Say so here rather than implying an id pins a model.

human_authorship.description: What a human contributed. Deliberately descriptive rather than a percentage: 'how much of this is human' has no unit, and inventing one would be the kind of laundered number law 5 exists to prevent.

description.description: e.g. 'the subject description, the style register and the exclusion list were written by a human; the pixels were not'.

synthetic_markers.description: FACTS about markers that are or are not present, and nothing else. Note what this object cannot do: a package saying 'watermark: none' has not been checked by anyone, and a package saying 'watermark: present' has not proved it. These are declarations, they are covered by the signature chain like every other byte, and a tool that treats them as detections is misreporting the file.

detectable_by.description: What would detect it, when anything would. Absent means the declarer does not know.

c2pa_manifest_present.description: Whether a C2PA manifest travels in this package. werk does not implement C2PA; see spec/X-C2PA-EXPORT.md for what the intended mapping is and, more importantly, for what it is not.

embedded_metadata_stripped.description: true when the producing pipeline is known to have dropped the original container metadata (EXIF, XMP, PNG text chunks). Worth stating: a reader finding no tEXt chunk in the PNG cannot otherwise tell 'never written' from 'removed'.

training_data_statement.description: What is known about what the model was trained on — which, for most models a reader will meet, is 'the operator has not disclosed it'. Recording that explicitly is the point: it turns an absence into a stated fact instead of an implication.

source.description: Where the statement came from — a published model card, a licence, the author's own training run. A training-data claim with no source is a rumour.

embedded_path.description: Path inside this package of the full statement, when it is carried. Law 1: a training-data statement that is a URL is a promise about another file.

subject.description: Facts about what the work depicts, limited to the ones that change how a viewer should read it. Deliberately small: this is not a content-rating system and must not grow into one.

fictional_universe.description: Named when the subject is fiction, so a viewer is not left to guess whether a person shown ever existed.

statements.description: Free-form additional declarations, each stamped with its own epistemic status (law 5) so a disclosure cannot smuggle a guess in beside a fact. Use this rather than inventing keys: an unknown key is a validation error, an unknown statement id is data a reader skips (law 12).

jurisdiction_note.description: OPTIONAL and INFORMATIONAL, and the schema will not let it become anything else. An author may record which regime they had in mind while writing these facts. It confers nothing: it is not a compliance claim, it does not bind a viewer, and a tool MUST NOT report a package as compliant with anything on the strength of it. The reason the field exists at all is that authors will otherwise write the same sentence into a note where no reader can find it.
